problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:
* Container 1: size 36 cubic meters, revenue $76
* Container 2: size 46 cubic meters, revenue $179
* Container 3: size 46 cubic meters, revenue $283
* Container 4: size 25 cubic meters, revenue $112
* Container 5: size 20 cubic meters, revenue $58
* Container 6: size 29 cubic meters, revenue $148
* Container 7: size 16 cubic meters, revenue $144
* Container 8: size 50 cubic meters, revenue $166
* Container 9: size 6 cubic meters, revenue $198
* Container 10: size 10 cubic meters, revenue $240
* Container 11: size 2 cubic meters, revenue $207
* Container 12: size 42 cubic meters, revenue $239
* Container 13: size 4 cubic meters, revenue $156
* Container 14: size 33 cubic meters, revenue $227
* Container 15: size 30 cubic meters, revenue $274
* Container 16: size 13 cubic meters, revenue $92
* Container 17: size 1 cubic meter, revenue $146
* Container 18: size 7 cubic meters, revenue $207
* Container 19: size 46 cubic meters, revenue $141
The vessel has a maximum capacity of 323 cubic meters. Choose the container combination that yields the highest total revenue without exceeding this capacity. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
